# Result: sensitivity grid, reconciliation, and recommended answer domain

## A. Completed sensitivity grid (student=1; online/anyone/community=0; missing handled 2 ways)
Granularity | Discipline | n | Miss-handling | **Computed orig %** | **Computed repl %** | MAE vs cited (pp)
--|--|--|--|--|--|--
STUDY-level | Social | 74 | as_nonstudent | **83.78** | **81.08** | **0.78**
ROWS-level | Social | 668 | exclude | 82.16 | 78.56 | 1.29
ROWS-level | Social | 668 | as_nonstudent | 82.04 | 78.44 | 1.41
STUDY-level | Social | 74 | exclude | 84.93 | 82.19 | 1.91
STUDY-level | Cognitive | 49 | exclude / as_nonstudent | 75.51 | 81.63 | 3.81
ROWS-level | Cognitive | 241 | exclude / as_nonstudent | 71.37 | 83.82 | 6.97
Economics (either granularity) | 18 | either | 94.44 | 100.00 | 15.57

**Single closest cell (per your criterion): study-level Social, missing row treated as non-student → original 83.8%, replication 81.1% (MAE 0.78pp).**

## B. Final cross-tabulation (study-level, 141 studies)
discipline x subjects.o: Social {students 62, anyone 7, community 4, NaN 1}; Cognitive {students 37, anyone 7, community 5}; Economics {students 17, community 1}.
discipline x subjects.r: Social {students 60, online 4, anyone 6, community 3, NaN 1}; Cognitive {students 40, online 0, anyone 3, community 6}; Economics {students 18}.

## C. Reconciliation (computed vs cited — kept distinct)
- **Primary/defensible operationalization** (study-level, rpp.154 excluded): Social **84.9% / 82.2%** — the closest discipline by a wide margin (MAE 1.9pp), vs Cognitive 75.5/81.6 (3.8) and Economics 94.4/100 (15.6).
- **Bounded range for the 1 missing study** (rpp.154): Social original ∈ [83.8%, 85.1%], replication ∈ [81.1%, 82.4%]. The cited 82.4/80.9 falls just below this interval (residual gap ≈ 1.4–2.5pp original, ≈ 0.2–1.3pp replication) — i.e., computed figures slightly overshoot the cited ones.
- **Robustness**: per-project splits (Social rpp 85.2/75.9, ml1 76.9/100, ml3 100/100) do not reproduce 82.4/80.9 either; pooled study-level Social is the best global match. Economics is unmistakably NOT the match — its 94.4/100 is the joint maximum but 15.6pp from the cited values, so per your instruction it is rejected as the answer.
- **Not used**: the second CSV (143×15, effect-size only) confirmed to contain no subject/domain columns; no author-name join attempted.

## D. Recommended single answer domain
**Social** — with computed student shares ≈ **83.8–84.9% (original)** and ≈ **81.1–82.2% (replication)** (best single cell 83.8/81.1), which best match the question's cited 82.4% / 80.9% under the approved operationalization (study-level dedup; students vs all-else binary; the one missing study bounded). Both shares are well above the 50% "primarily" bar; no other discipline comes close.

**Proposed final hypothesis (awaiting your authorization to submit):** "The domain in which **both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects** is **Social (Psychology/Social science)**. Computed from the study-level data, ~83.8–84.9% of original studies and ~81.1–82.2% of replication studies in the Social domain used students, the closest match to the cited 82.4% / 80.9%; Economics — despite having the highest student share (94.4%/100%) — does not match the cited figures, and Cognitive is lower still."
